It's common knowledge that GamerGate activity hubs such as /r/KotakuInAction and the GG-related boards of 8chan are populated with members very sympathetic to the men's movement, as opposed to the internet at large. People like Milo Yiannopoulos and Christina Hoff Sommers are "household names" in these communities, and Men's Rights topics such as the UVA Rape case are frequently discussed.

While the primary focus of GamerGate is of course ethics in the video game community, much attention is also spent exposing and breaking down SJW and radical feminist narratives. Is the addressal of these narratives only an auxiliary focus, or something more? By exposing the radical leftist presence as a cover for corruption and collusion in the gaming subculture, has GamerGate helped equip it's members with the tools to call out radical leftism in other environments? Will victories for GamerGate naturally open doors for the discussion of Men's Right's issues?

The traffic information available on the /r/MensRights subreddit is inconclusive, but in the purely subjective opinion of someone who has browsed the sub for more than two years, it seems as though the subreddit has grown increasingly more active during the course of GamerGate. I'm not one to espouse that correlation = causation, but the fact that so many people have been drawn to a movement which is far more educated on and sympathetic towards the men's movement than the internet at large seems a likely explanation. Crossposting, inter-sub discussion, and "dual citizenship" redditors all serve to introduce a new audience to Men's rights discussions and topics.

It seems clear that GamerGate is a very positive thing for the Men's movement; once feminist narratives on gender are rejected, other explanations and perspectives can gain a lot more ground. If GamerGate can weather the storm of constant media attacks and grow in size and repute to become a sufficient counterweight to the feminist and SJW presence in gaming, can MRA's expect to "ride it's thermals", so to speak? Furthermore, does GamerGate stop with gaming, or is this just the beginning? Will we continue to identify and root out the radical leftist presence in other areas of our culture as well? If so, then can we expect a turning point in the gender discussion to follow?
Is, and to what extent is the GamerGate movement opening doors for discussion of Men's Rights issues?
